answer: An agent market can require each identity to bond tokens before it can take paid work, with disputes able to slash that bond. Splitting one agent into a thousand Sybils does not create more economic weight: each must lock fresh capital, and dishonest identities risk losing it. The bond is an anchor for accountability; reputation grows from completed work, not names, so a fake-identity spiral ties up funds without multiplying trust. Like nectar, the reward attracts agents, but the bond makes fraud costly.
